Hi there, thanks for sending that over. I notice the records jump from the seller’s purchase at 48,000 miles directly to tires at 75,000, with zero documentation for the CVT transmission—Nissan’s most critical and notoriously failure-prone component during this era. CVT fluid service or at minimum a diagnostic health check is required every 30k–60k miles to prevent catastrophic failure. The complete omission of this from the service history, combined with third-party flags regarding concealed transmission diagnostics, indicates a high probability of imminent CVT degradation or latent failure.

Per my acquisition protocol, I deduct the full estimated cost of unverified critical defects from market value. A 2016 Altima CVT replacement or major rebuild runs $3,500–$4,200 at reputable independent or dealership shops. Using the KBB private-party baseline of $11,765 and subtracting the full $4,000 CVT risk/repair cost, I’m prepared to offer **$7,800**. 

This reflects a fair, market-adjusted price for the vehicle as-is, accounting for the immediate likelihood of costly transmission intervention. If Michael can provide certified documentation of proper CVT fluid service history or a passed transmission health diagnostic from a Nissan-qualified technician, I’m open to an upward adjustment. Until then, $7,800 is my firm baseline. Let me know if this aligns with his expectations.
